stories.title: BUB signaling in cancer and molecular insights into targeted therapies
stories.description: The Spindle Assembly Checkpoint (SAC) is vital for proper chromosome segregation during cell division and for maintaining genomic integrity; its disruption can cause aneuploidy and tumors. The BUB gene family ensures SAC fidelity by regulating kinetochore–microtubule attachments and mitotic progression. Dysregulation leads to chromosomal instability (CIN), contributing to cancer progression, heterogeneity, metastasis, and therapy resistance. Beyond mitosis, BUB proteins influence DNA repair, chromatin remodeling, transcription, and immune responses. They interact with cell cycle and genome stability pathways, impacting cancer prognosis and therapy response. Research is ongoing to validate BUB proteins as biomarkers and develop inhibitors, possibly combined with immunotherapies or DNA-damaging agents for resistant tumors. This review  summarizes their functions, highlighting their potential in personalized cancer treatment. This Review examines the diverse roles of BUB proteins in chromosome segregation, cancer progression, and therapy resistance. It highlights emerging therapeutic strategies and future directions for targeting BUB signaling in cancer.

stories.title: Artificial intelligence for life-cycle-aware sustainable materials discovery
stories.description: Artificial intelligence has accelerated the discovery of new materials, offering a route towards sustainable development. Candidates are nevertheless evaluated almost exclusively on functional performance. Whether a material can be manufactured at scale, how it behaves once built into a real product, what burden its production places on the environment and what becomes of it at the end of its life are questions addressed only after the choice has been settled, when little can be altered. Bringing these considerations into the discovery process itself is achievable and would yield materials that are sustainable not by accident but by design. Materials discovery by artificial intelligence rarely considers scalability, environmental impacts or end-of-life management, prioritizing functional performance. This Perspective suggests a roadmap for embedding life-cycle considerations in the discovery process to design sustainable materials from the start.

stories.title: Synthesis of covalent organic frameworks through hydrogen-bonding catalysis
stories.description: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are a class of crystalline, porous networks constructed by polymerization of organic building blocks. However, most COF syntheses developed so far rely on acid- or base-catalysed reactions that are sensitive to monomer structure, require extensive condition screening, proceed under harsh conditions over several days and often yield low-quality products. Here we report a general hydrogen-bonding catalysis strategy enabled by benzimidazole and its derivatives, acting as both hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors, to produce high-quality COFs. Distinct from conventional catalysis, these catalysts interact with monomers, intermediates and transition states, thereby reducing energy barriers at each step and promoting reversibility. This approach enables control through catalyst-to-monomer ratios and allows the rapid synthesis, within hours, of imide-, imine-, hydrazone- and sp2-carbon-linked COFs with high crystallinity and porosity. The method further supports catalyst reuse and 1,000-fold scale-up, producing COFs with benchmark proton conductivity, establishing hydrogen-bonding catalysis as a versatile route for scalable COF synthesis and applications. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are typically synthesized under harsh acid- or base-catalysed conditions. Here a hydrogen-bonding catalysis strategy based on reusable benzimidazole enables the rapid and scalable production of COFs with high crystallinity and porosity, offering a general route to imide, imine, hydrazone and sp2-carbon-linked COF synthesis.

stories.title: Identification of critical timing when abnormal weather affects maize and soft wheat yields in Italy using functional quantile regression
stories.description: In this study, we apply functional regression analysis to identify the specific within-season periods during which temperature and precipitation anomalies most affect cereal yields. Using provincial data for Italy from 1952 to 2023, we analyze two major cereals, maize and soft wheat, and quantify how abnormal weather conditions influence yields across the growing cycle. Unlike traditional statistical yield models, which assume additive temperature effects over the season, our approach is capable of capturing the timing and functional shape of weather impacts. In particular, the results show that above-average temperatures reduce maize yields primarily during the phases from stem elongation to grain filling (June to August), with the peak placed during flowering (mid July). For soft wheat, the unusually high temperatures have a generally negative impact on yields, particularly during the stem elongation phase (from late March to early April). Precipitation also exerts season-dependent effects, improving wheat yields early in the season but reducing them later on. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for intra-seasonal weather patterns to provide insights for climate change adaptation strategies, including the timely adjustment of key crop management inputs.

stories.title: RailMASDet: a 3D object detection method for railway LiDAR point cloud foreign object detection
stories.description: To address the issues of easy loss and inaccurate localization of distant small targets in railway LiDAR point cloud foreign object detection, this paper proposes a 3D object detection method named RailMASDet. The method constructs a cross-scale semantic spatial feature reassembly strategy. By employing transposed restoration of deep features and aligned compression of shallow features, it resolves the problem of spatial detail loss of distant targets in deep BEV feature maps. Furthermore, a railway-oriented channel modulation strategy based on existing channel attention mechanisms is introduced. By jointly exploiting global average and maximum statistics, the strategy adaptively enhances object-sensitive responses and suppresses structured-background interference in railway BEV features. Meanwhile, a foreground probability-driven non-Euclidean distance sampling paradigm is established, embedding point-level foreground priors into the distance metric function to shift keypoint sampling from uniform coverage to semantically guided targeted focusing. On the OSDaR23 dataset, RailMASDet achieves AP0.7 of 80.59% for pedestrians and 70.05% for car, and an mAP0.5 of 76.56%, outperforming the baseline model by 4.95, 3.78, and 3.21 percentage points, respectively. The average center localization error of detection boxes is 0.86 m, which is 57.5% lower than that of the baseline. The inference latency is 276.5 ms per frame, demonstrating reasonable computational efficiency. Ablation studies and visualization analyses validate the individual contributions of the three modules and their synergistic enhancement effects, confirming that the proposed method can effectively solve the problems of small target loss and insufficient localization accuracy in railway foreign object detection, thereby demonstrating its potential for long-range foreign object detection in sparse railway LiDAR scenes.

stories.title: Palaeoclimate constraints narrow uncertainty in future Arctic winter sea ice projections
stories.description: Arctic sea ice decline has been observed across all seasons and is projected to continue in the future. Relative to historical observations, climate models show their largest biases and uncertainties during winter, when ice cover strongly regulates air–sea heat exchange, ocean mixing and atmospheric circulation. Palaeoclimate records offer opportunities to evaluate model performance beyond the historical period, but applications have remained largely qualitative. Here we compile an Arctic-wide database of mid-Holocene (5–7 thousand years ago) biomarkers to assess sea ice simulations of this past warm period. Using a recently developed proxy system model, we present a Bayesian palaeoclimate model weighting scheme that refines the multi-model mean winter sea ice extent through fully quantitative proxy-model comparisons, accounting for model interdependence and non-stationary proxy seasonality. We demonstrate that, by adjusting the contribution of each model to the ensemble mean based on proxy evidence, model weights can eliminate biases and reduce uncertainties by 85%, to the level of interannual variability. Weighted projections using the same climate models indicate that future winter sea ice extent may be nearly 1 million km2 lower than prior estimates across forthcoming decades and possible emissions scenarios, with broad implications for Arctic ecosystems, mid-latitude weather, and cryosphere stability. Forecasts of future Arctic Ocean sea ice loss can be substantially improved using Holocene proxy records by applying a model weighting approach.

stories.title: Circulating chromatin reveals effects of disease-associated variants on gene regulation
stories.description: A fundamental challenge in human genetics is determining how regulatory genetic variation shapes complex traits and disease risk. Chromatin quantitative trait loci can link disease-associated variants to regulatory element activity, but mapping them in disease-relevant tissues at scale remains challenging. We leverage epigenomic liquid biopsy by profiling histone modifications in circulating chromatin from 328 cancer patients and 38 healthy individuals to identify cell-free chromatin quantitative trait loci. These loci affect regulatory element activities from diverse non-hematologic tissues and developmentally restricted elements reactivated in cancer. Through cistrome-wide association studies, we link 4891 loci to 1011 traits and diseases. Developmentally restricted loci absent in white blood cells are associated with 22.7 traits per 100 quantitative trait loci, compared to 0.58 for white-blood-cell-restricted chromatin quantitative trait loci. Here, we show that cell-free chromatin enables efficient and scalable discovery of regulatory genetic effects across tissues, diseases, and populations. Regulatory genetic variants can influence disease risk through effects on chromatin activity, but studying these effects across tissues remains challenging. Here, the authors use cell‑free chromatin profiling to identify chromatin quantitative trait loci across diverse tissues, linking regulatory variation to hundreds of human traits and diseases.

stories.title: Depression, functional disability, and cardiovascular disease in adults with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages 0–3: a nationally representative cohort study
stories.description: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome (CKM) has emerged as an integrated framework for identifying individuals at increased cardiovascular risk before clinical cardiovascular disease (CVD) develops. However, whether psychological and functional vulnerabilities further refine risk stratification in earlier CKM stages remains unclear. Using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, we examined the joint association of depression and functional disability with incident CVD among 7217 adults with CKM stages 0–3. Participants were categorized into four groups according to baseline depression and functional disability status. During follow-up, incident CVD, heart disease, and stroke were assessed. Compared with participants with neither depression nor functional disability, those with depression only, functional disability only, and both conditions had higher risks of incident CVD in fully adjusted Cox models, with the highest risk observed among participants with both conditions. Similar patterns were observed for heart disease and stroke. No statistically significant additive or multiplicative interactions were found between depression and functional disability. Adding depression and functional disability to conventional risk factors modestly improved CVD risk prediction. These findings suggest that depression and functional disability should be considered as important dimensions in CVD risk assessment for adults with CKM stages 0–3, supporting a more comprehensive approach to early cardiovascular risk stratification.

stories.title: Hypertensive stress rewires macrophage signaling in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction independent of obesity
stories.description: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains a major unmet clinical challenge. Although obesity is common in many HFpEF cohorts from Europe and North America, three Japanese HFpEF cohorts identified hypertension and sympathetic overactivation, rather than obesity, as dominant features. To model these features, we established an HFpEF mouse model in which sympathetic activation induces hypertensive heart disease, while endothelial dysfunction acts as a second hit driving progression to HFpEF. Hypertensive stress rewires cardiac macrophage-derived intercellular signaling, impairing macrophage-to-cardiomyocyte BMP signaling and fatty acid oxidation while enhancing macrophage-to-fibroblast PDGF signaling, thereby promoting metabolic remodeling, inflammation, and fibrosis. ANGPTL2 inhibition preserves macrophage intercellular communication and prevents HFpEF development. These findings identify cardiac macrophage signaling rewiring as a central mechanism linking hypertensive stress to metabolic remodeling and inflammation, revealing a pathogenic pathway for HFpEF in the absence of obesity that is distinct from HFpEF associated with obesity. Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction can occur without obesity. Here, the authors show that it is common in Japanese cohorts and find in mice that hypertensive stress alters macrophage signaling, promoting metabolic remodeling and inflammation.
